subject: William Wilberforce and the 1833 abolition settlement
timeline: Anti-Slavery Society founded; parliamentary leadership passed to Thomas Fowell Buxton
Abolitionist electoral campaign; Samuel Sharpe executed May 23
Act took effect in covered colonies

gates.taken: Forced labor, liberty and control of earnings
gates.removed: Freedom of movement and occupational and family autonomy
gates.suffered: Violence, coercion, deprivation and compulsory apprenticeship
gates.who: Trace specific enslavers, operators, merchants and state decisions; Wilberforce was a reform advocate, retired before passage
gates.why: Profit and plantation interests; compensation compromise to secure abolition; individual motives require evidence

domains.finance: Compensation allocated to owners, not enslaved people
domains.legal: Abolition and transitional compulsory apprenticeship; geographic exceptions
domains.it: Recordkeeping and claim registers; historical information systems
domains.healthcare: Physical injury and coercion; individual records needed
domains.labor: Unpaid forced work and subsequent apprenticeship
domains.resources: Plantations, land, production assets; individual ownership histories unresolved

auditors.Jane: Trace labor, capital and compensation flows
auditors.Toph: Distinguish emancipation from restitution and Wilberforce from later legislators
auditors.Patricia: National Archives T71 and AO14 underpin UCL database; do not count derivatives as independent witnesses. Bank ledgers document separate payment events.

pop: Cessation of harm does not equal restitution.
limitations: No individual claims or original payroll inspected; no modern liability or damages assigned. Three auditors are analytical roles, not independent witnesses.
